shelves.title: Meaning, wonder & spiritual curiosity
shelves.intro: A conversation, some context, or a bigger question. You do not need a new identity to begin.

shelves.title: Attention & a less punishing inner life
shelves.intro: Explore one optional practice. There is no course to finish and no ideal state to achieve.

shelves.title: Understand AI without making it your life
shelves.intro: Start with a useful explanation, not a new subscription. Vendor lessons are identified as such.

shelves.title: Technology that returns you to the world
shelves.intro: Notice something, borrow a book, and let the tool remain a small part of the experience.

shelves.title: People, memory & showing up
shelves.intro: Tools for listening, remembering, and making ordinary participation easier.

shelves.title: Thinking, reading & seeing differently
shelves.intro: Not everything here is a method for improvement. Some things are worth encountering for their own sake.

resources.title: On Being: a conversation about attention
resources.creator: The On Being Project
resources.requirements: Free web audio and transcript; no subscription needed for this selection.
resources.why: A way into meaning through a person and a conversation rather than a list of conclusions. The selected interview connects creative work with attention to the world.
resources.start: Open the Mary Oliver conversation and choose audio or the transcript. You can begin with a short passage.
resources.limit: A personal conversation, not a universal spiritual teaching.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: Religious traditions, with context
resources.creator: Harvard University, The Pluralism Project
resources.requirements: Free public essays; no registration needed to read.
resources.why: Spiritual vocabulary means more when it is connected to the people and histories that use it. This collection helps provide that context.
resources.start: Read Rivers of Faith, then choose one tradition that you would like to understand better.
resources.limit: The project has an American context. Traditions are not interchangeable or internally uniform.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: A landscape of consciousness
resources.creator: Closer To Truth
resources.requirements: Free public introduction; no registration needed to read.
resources.why: For a larger question after an ordinary one: how does felt experience relate to the world we can describe? This is an orientation to different proposed answers.
resources.start: Begin with Exploring Consciousness rather than trying to navigate the entire theory map.
resources.limit: This is a broad taxonomy, not a ranking of evidence or proof that all proposals are equally supported.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: A brief guided pause
resources.creator: UCLA Mindful, UCLA Health
resources.requirements: Free web audio; transcripts for some recordings. An app is optional.
resources.why: A straightforward starting point without needing another subscription. The recordings let you explore a practice rather than commit to an entire program.
resources.start: Find the three-minute Body and Sound Meditation in the English list, or choose a language and format that suits you.
resources.limit: An optional practice, not a treatment promise. Skip or stop anything uncomfortable; keep essential care and access needs intact.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: Awe Outing
resources.creator: Greater Good Science Center, UC Berkeley
resources.requirements: Free practice instructions; optional accounts support saving and participation.
resources.why: A prompt for approaching familiar surroundings with curiosity. Its written format offers another way in besides guided audio.
resources.start: Read the instructions and choose an accessible setting that already fits your day.
resources.limit: Keep necessary devices available despite the source's suggestion to put them away. No special feeling is required.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: Practice in a named tradition
resources.creator: Plum Village App
resources.entry_title: Plum Village app and sample audio
resources.requirements: The provider offers the app and its content free; optional donations. A sample recording is on the website.
resources.why: An example of technology carrying a contemplative tradition. It belongs alongside, not in place of, secular and other spiritual approaches.
resources.start: Explore the public sample and background before deciding whether to install the app.
resources.limit: This offering has a specific Buddhist context. It is not a neutral ranking of spiritual practices.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: How AI Works
resources.creator: Code.org
resources.requirements: Free public videos and lesson material; no account needed for the introductory video page.
resources.why: A low-commitment explanation before choosing an AI tool. Classroom framing does not prevent an adult newcomer from using the introductory material.
resources.start: Start with Introducing How AI Works at the top of the page, not the full lesson sequence.
resources.limit: Designed for education. Separate learning about AI from deciding whether a particular tool fits your task.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: OpenAI Academy
resources.creator: OpenAI
resources.requirements: Courses are free. A ChatGPT account is required to start a course and save progress.
resources.why: A direct source for learning how the provider expects its tools to be used. It can support a practical task without making training the main project.
resources.start: Browse the course list first; choose an introductory AI Foundations option rather than an advanced workflow.
resources.limit: Vendor-authored education. Free training does not mean every demonstrated product feature is free.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: Getting started with Claude
resources.creator: Anthropic, Claude Academy
resources.requirements: The selected written tutorial is free to read. Course progress and using Claude have separate sign-in requirements.
resources.why: A short provider-authored introduction for readers who want to understand a first request before exploring more advanced tools.
resources.start: Read the first-prompt section. Use fictional, non-sensitive information when trying an example.
resources.limit: Vendor-authored education; feature access depends on the product and plan, not the tutorial's price.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: Merlin Bird ID
resources.creator: Cornell Lab of Ornithology
resources.requirements: Free app; email confirmation is required for continued use. Download only through the official links.
resources.why: A small way to connect an unfamiliar bird with a question you can investigate. The identification is the beginning of noticing, not the end.
resources.start: Read the official setup guide and check the identification support for your region.
resources.limit: Suggestions can be wrong, and Sound ID coverage varies by region. No credit card is required by Merlin.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: Seek by iNaturalist
resources.creator: iNaturalist
resources.requirements: Free app; no registration required for basic use.
resources.why: Image recognition can help you ask better questions about something already nearby, rather than give you another reason to keep scrolling.
resources.start: Read about the app before installing. Try observing one thing without needing to collect badges.
resources.limit: Optional iNaturalist sign-in and posting change data sharing. Never use identification guesses to decide what is safe to eat or touch.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: Borrow something with Libby
resources.creator: OverDrive and participating libraries
resources.requirements: Free borrowing with an eligible card at a participating library. Titles and waits vary by library.
resources.why: Sometimes the most useful technology simply gets a book into reach. There is no need to turn reading into a course or a reading challenge.
resources.start: Find your library and browse what is available before choosing a title. The web version is an option on supported browsers.
resources.limit: Library eligibility, collection, and availability are local. A particular book is not guaranteed.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: A question for a real conversation
resources.creator: StoryCorps
resources.requirements: Free public question bank. Recording or uploading is not required to use it.
resources.why: A useful starting point when you want to hear more from someone but do not know where to begin. The value can remain in the conversation itself.
resources.start: Choose one question from Great Questions for Anyone and ask whether the person would enjoy discussing it.
resources.limit: Agreement to talk is not permission to record, upload, or publish. Skip intrusive questions.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: Keep a digital story findable
resources.creator: Library of Congress
resources.why: A story is easier to revisit when its file is understandable and findable. This resource supports the quiet work after recording or writing.
resources.start: Choose the guidance for the kind of material you actually have, such as photos or audio.
resources.limit: Some platform examples are older. Use the preservation principles and check current device instructions separately.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: Visual assistance and human help
resources.creator: Be My Eyes
resources.requirements: Free personal-use app with setup/sign-in. Commercial offerings and optional hardware are separate.
resources.why: A concrete example of technology supporting access: blind and low-vision users can seek visual assistance from people and AI. There is also a volunteering route.
resources.start: Read the personal app overview and choose the assistance or volunteering path relevant to you.
resources.limit: Follow the service's usage limits. AI descriptions are not a substitute for appropriate help in consequential or unsafe situations.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: A first encounter with philosophy
resources.creator: The Open University, OpenLearn
resources.requirements: Free course text can be started without registration; progress, quizzes, and participation features use an account.
resources.why: An invitation to examine arguments rather than collect impressive names. You can sample the activity of philosophy without adopting a complete system.
resources.start: Open the Introduction or Approaching philosophy section. The full course is optional.
resources.limit: An older introductory course, not current scientific reporting or a promise of personal transformation.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: The Evolution of Trust
resources.creator: Nicky Case
resources.why: A playful way to examine how simplified rules affect cooperation. It connects questions about decisions with the limits of models.
resources.start: Try the opening interaction. For a text-only route, use the companion decision essay below.
resources.limit: The public entry page was checked, not a full interactive playthrough. This is a toy model, not a guide to judging people.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.

resources.title: Poetry Unbound: one poem at a time
resources.creator: The On Being Project; hosted by Pádraig Ó Tuama
resources.requirements: Free episode audio and transcript; books and other offerings are separate.
resources.why: A different kind of attention, with no task to optimize. This selection leaves room for an unexpected moment to matter without pretending it fixes everything.
resources.start: Open Wonder Woman and choose the recording or transcript. It is fine simply to listen.
resources.limit: The episode discusses chronic pain and contains some strong language. No health benefit is promised.
resources.review_scope: Public page and provider access information reviewed; app use, course completion, and media playback are not independently verified.
